topic: Hiccups: 68-year record, glottis snap, fetal hiccups, gill reflex theory
caption:
Charles Osborne got the hiccups in 1922 while lifting a hog and didn't stop until 1990. Guinness World Records counts it as the longest attack ever, an estimated 430 million hics.

Every hiccup is a diaphragm spasm followed by your vocal cords snapping shut. You even did it in the womb. Scientists still aren't sure why, and one theory traces it back to gill breathing. Hiccups lasting over 48 hours are worth a doctor's visit. Sources: Guinness World Records, Mayo Clinic, Straus et al. (BioEssays, 2003).

What's your go-to hiccup cure, and does it actually work?

2/4 What a hiccup is (35 ms)
Your diaphragm spasms and pulls in air. Your vocal cords slam shut a split second later. That's the 'hic'.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/4 It starts in the womb
Ultrasounds show babies hiccuping long before birth. Newborns hiccup far more often than adults do.
🎨 AI-generated image

4/4 Nobody knows why (Gills)
One theory: it's a leftover reflex from amphibian ancestors, who pumped water over gills with their airways shut.
